newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Palm oil ship bound for Europe delayed by cleaning.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil ship bound for Europe delayed by cleaning.

text.p: A contaminated edible oils tanker has caused a mild squeeze on palm oil supplies to Europe after the vessel was delayed to allow workers to clean it before loading, a trader at a Singapore-based commodity house said.
"The ship was not clean. They found traces of other vegetable oils which the ship was carrying previously," the trader told Reuters on Wednesday.
"It (the ship) has to be inspected and cleaned up properly before loading this 20,000 to 25,000 tonnes -- a mixture of palm oil, palm kernel and coconut oil," he said.
The trader declined to provide details of the ship, where it is currently located, the time it has been delayed or when it is expected to sail.
"It is somewhere in the Strait of Malacca and is still being cleaned up," he said.
"This is the problem that has caused delay in loading the vessel to Europe, resulting in the tightness in nearby supply for November."

Following news of the shipment delay on Tuesday, crude palm oil CIF Europe closed US$7.50 to $12.50 a tonne higher after the December position traded from $562.50 up to $575, March at $550 and January at $557.50 and $560.
European traders said the delay had pushed prices higher because it would cause a supply gap and shipments would have to be pushed back.

But the squeeze in nearby positions for Europe had no impact on Kuala Lumpur Commodity Exchange crude palm oil futures or on physical palm oil prices in the Malaysian market on Wednesday, traders said.
-- Tan Lee Lee, Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230-7510)
